name: Commit Message Writer
description: Reads git diffs and produces well-structured conventional commit messages following the Conventional Commits specification (type(scope): description, optional body and footer)

conventional-format.description: Produces commit messages that follow the Conventional Commits specification with correct type, optional scope, and description

tests.description: Recognizes a new feature diff and produces a feat: commit
Recognizes a bug fix diff and produces a fix: commit
Only uses valid conventional commit types
tests.prompt:
Write a commit message for this diff:

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -1,5 +1,10 @@
 # MyProject
 
-A simple project.
+A powerful CLI tool for managing deployments.
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+npm install -g myproject
+```

diff-comprehension.description: Accurately understands the semantic meaning of git diffs and reflects it in the commit message

tests.description: Summarizes a multi-file diff accurately without listing every file
Identifies refactoring changes vs functional changes
Does not invent changes not present in the diff
tests.prompt:
Write a commit message for this diff:

diff --git a/tsconfig.json b/tsconfig.json
--- a/tsconfig.json
+++ b/tsconfig.json
@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@
     "target": "ES2020",
-    "strict": false,
+    "strict": true,
     "outDir": "./dist"
   }
 }

message-quality.description: Produces concise, informative commit messages with appropriate subject line length and optional body

tests.description: Subject line is concise (under ~72 chars) and lowercase after type prefix
Uses imperative mood in the subject line (add, fix, change — not added, fixed, changed)

git-diff-reading.description: Can request and read git diffs via tool calls when not provided inline

tests.description: Calls a shell tool to get git diff when no diff is provided
tests.prompt: Write a commit message for the currently staged changes.

tests.description: Uses an appropriate git diff command
tests.prompt: I just staged some files. Generate a commit message for them.
